geo.title: What to know
geo.body:
Practice the lessons so far, then check your answers.

Goal: I can perform and describe single transformations.

  • 3.1 I can describe a transformation as a rule that moves every point.
  • 3.2 I can translate a figure by a vector and describe it with coordinates.
  • 3.3 I can reflect a figure and explain why the mirror line is the perpendicular bisector of each segment joining a point to its image.
  • 3.4 I can rotate a figure about any center by a given angle.
  • 3.5 I can show that two reflections make a translation or a rotation.
  • 3.6 I can describe a sequence of rigid motions that maps one figure onto another.
  • 3.7 I can explain why rigid motions preserve lengths and angle measures.
  • 3.9 I can find all lines of symmetry of a figure.
  • 3.10 I can identify rotational and point symmetry.
  • 3.11 I can describe the symmetries in a pattern.
  • 3.12 I can define congruent figures as figures related by a sequence of rigid motions.

slides.title: Practice: 3.1
slides.html: Under a transformation, does a point that is not on the shape move?
slides.reveal: Yes, every point of the plane has an image. The shape just shows us some of them.

slides.title: Common traps
slides.html:
Watch out for these common mistakes:

  • a rotation is always about the origin
  • a reflection line must be vertical or horizontal
  • order of transformations never matters
  • a translation "moves the shape" rather than every point
